description: Fire Triangle is a team based in Vancouver ready to protect the safety of future space missions through the power of machine learning. Our team shares a passion for space exploration and designing interactive programs.
summary:
FlamePredict is an interactive, SI-powered website that uses the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) dataset and AI analysis to decode how fire behaves in microgravity and partial-gravity environments such as the moon base. Our goal is to help space exploration researchers design safer spacecraft and lunar habitats, and to raise awareness about the importance of fire safety in space among the general public. FlamePredict not only ranks current experiments in terms of relevance to moon base and fire safety research, but also features an interactive 3D model of microgravity fire.

FlamePredict addresses the challenge of complex and fragmented scientific data by making understanding fire safety in space easier than ever before. By empowering space exploration to the moon and beyond, FlamePredict aims to ensure that every astronaut can come home safe.
details:
FlamePredict was developed using React.js to create the main dashboard and the overall structure of our website. Three.js was used to render the interactive 3D microgravity fire simulation directly in the browser. For super intelligence, NASA's PSI database, along with the E-FIELD Flames experiment was fed into Claude to summarize and rank the experiments based on relevance to fire safety research.

Readers are able to select a section of the website text and provide comment/feedback that can be viewed by anyone accessing the website. This ensures the website is up to date with state-of-the-art research in space exploration.

The user interface was designed with a layout that prioritizes making the experimental data easy-to-read and understandable. This was achieved by displaying graphs for each experiment (oxygen, pressure, and airflow used in the study), making dense physics intuitive and accessible across both desktop and mobile devices.

Overall, by creating a visualization of experiment data, ranking the experiments, and even an interactive 3D model of microgravity fire, understanding fire safety in space became easier than ever-before.
